parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure Node.js ESM `.mjs` files, local imports only, manual `--a` parsing, Python `int()` behavior, `bucketize` group order, and exact `print` formatting.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Despite swarm mode being enabled, the main actor explicitly chose not to spawn subagents because the task was small and kept implementation, fixes, verification, and final response under one owner.
parallel.implementation: Observed executable behavior, wrote `bucketize`, `pyformat`, `argparse`, `pyint`, and `test5.mjs`, then fixed option-like argument handling and changed integer parsing/parity to BigInt after finding precision drift.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated all local ESM modules under `/output/lib` and `/output/test5.mjs`; status artifact validation lists the expected entry file and supporting modules as copied successfully.
parallel.verification: Ran direct comparisons against the executable for normal values, order-sensitive groups, whitespace, errors, negative-option edge cases, and arbitrary-precision integers before finalizing; official evaluation passed 144/144.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished or incorrect behavior remained; final notes mention only expected program-name/PyInstaller runtime-artifact differences outside task logic.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, `.mjs`, no-dependency, manual CLI parsing, bucketize parity, Python repr, and executable-observation requirements from the shared prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single serial main actor for all work, first probing behavior extensively, then writing modules, adjusting argparse behavior, and running a final sweep.
serial.implementation: Created `pybuiltins`, `iterutils`, `pyformat`, `argparse`, and `test5.mjs`; it emphasized argparse edge cases including repeated `--a`, unrecognized extras, negative-number matching, help text, and the bare `--` separator.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated a larger local ESM module set under `/output/lib` and `/output/test5.mjs`; status artifact validation reports the expected entry and support files were collected successfully.
serial.verification: Ran many executable-vs-node comparisons, corrected the `--` behavior, and performed a final comprehensive sweep; official evaluation passed 144/144.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished or incorrect behavior remained; remaining self-reported diffs were PyInstaller runtime crash lines and program-name differences rather than task logic.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode main actor saw the full prompt requiring ESM `.mjs`, manual `--a` parsing, no external dependencies, bucketize behavior, and output parity.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor received the byte-identical prompt and addressed the same CLI, formatting, module, dependency, and executable-observation requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference is evidenced; both satisfied the official evaluator, though the serial run explored more argparse edge cases manually.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Swarm mode was injected, but the main actor explicitly stated it would handle the small single-file task directly instead of spawning subagents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used one main actor throughout, with serial status showing no swarm mode and no delegation activity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both were effectively single-owner attempts; the parallel-mode run differed only by having swarm mode available and declined, not by executing parallel decomposition.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child briefs, child handoffs, or cross-agent interface contracts; the main actor wrote local modules and the entry file itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were likewise no child briefs or handoffs; module interfaces were designed within the single main actor's serial implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No cross-agent context transfer difference exists. Any interface choices were local implementation decisions in both runs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel-mode implementation started with executable probes, wrote four library modules plus `test5.mjs`, fixed argparse option-like values, then switched to BigInt after detecting large integer precision mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implementation probed more edge cases before and after writing files, created a broader argparse replica, adjusted the bare `--` behavior, and delivered a passing module tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation paths differ in depth and focus: parallel converged faster through a BigInt correction, while serial spent more steps on argparse fidelity; both were accepted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child result lifecycle existed. The main actor consumed its own tool results, applied fixes, and ended with a final completion response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child result lifecycle existed in serial either. Tool results returned directly to the main actor and were used for subsequent edits and finalization.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no join, trapped result, ignored child result, or lifecycle divergence; both closed after main-actor verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The main actor wrote `/output/lib/bucketize.mjs`, `pyformat.mjs`, `argparse.mjs`, `pyint.mjs`, then `/output/test5.mjs`, with later same-owner edits for fixes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor created `/output/lib` and wrote `pybuiltins.mjs`, `iterutils.mjs`, `pyformat.mjs`, `argparse.mjs`, and `test5.mjs` as one-owner workspace changes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision is evidenced. Parallel produced a slightly different helper-module split, but without concurrent writes or provenance ambiguity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel-mode verification included executable comparisons for core, error, negative value, and BigInt cases, followed by an official evaluator pass of 144/144.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification included a broader manual sweep of argparse cases and also ended with an official evaluator pass of 144/144.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had more manual exploratory verification, but neither verification path left an official acceptance gap; both official outcomes are complete passes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode attempt completed in 266.357 agent seconds with 13 LLM requests, did not time out, and closed after reporting successful verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt completed in 636.469 agent seconds with 22 LLM requests, did not time out, and closed after a final comprehensive comparison sweep.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial used substantially more time and requests, but this was not an adverse closure problem because both stayed within budget and passed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: parallel and serial each passed 144 of 144 samples. The only task-solving difference is process shape: the parallel-mode run had swarm mode enabled but did not execute any subagent or multi-agent mechanism, then completed a direct implementation with targeted fixes; the serial run performed a longer single-actor exploration and final sweep. Both delivered accepted modular ESM solutions, so no parallel coordination error explains an outcome gap.
parallel_contributors: Swarm mode was available but not used; the main actor retained direct ownership and completed the solution.
The parallel run fixed a discovered arbitrary-precision integer mismatch before closure.
serial_contributors: The serial run stayed single-actor and explored argparse behavior more extensively before finalizing.
The serial run adjusted its parser after discovering the executable's handling of bare `--` extras.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used a smaller helper split with `pyint.mjs` and BigInt parity; serial used a larger `argparse.mjs`/`pybuiltins.mjs` design and more edge-case probes.
Self-reported remaining differences in both runs were runtime program-name or PyInstaller traceback artifacts, not official evaluator failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both current completed official evaluations passed
